inventory.name: text-overflow: ellipsis clip-on-user-interaction — the ellipsis is replaced by clip while the user interacts with the element

syntax.rationale: The change adds no grammar, property or flag: #at-a-glance reads 'Status: Platform behaviour change (no new CSS property)' and 'Flag: None', and the record's feature_type is 'Chromium catches up'. The declaration surface this page turns on is therefore the existing declarations named in this section's 'Affected elements' row — 'overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis' — plus the temporary 'clip' mode the 'Chrome 149+' row switches them to, which §ellipsis-interaction is the grammar for ('the user agent may treat text-overflow: ellipsis as text-overflow: clip' while interacting). Same ruling as the B1 sibling contract for this feature and the B3 indexeddb unit: when a change declares no new grammar, the declarations the change acts on are the syntax surface.

inputs.rationale: The inputs are the two preconditions this section states: the three declarations above present on the element, and a user gesture — 'When the user focuses, clicks, or moves the caret inside such an element, the overflow mode temporarily switches to clip'. Nothing is passed from script and nothing is opt-in: the record's browsers.chrome.flag and browsers.chrome.origintrial are both false, and its feature_type is 'Chromium catches up'.

outputs.rationale: The output is a rendering change, not a return value: the 'Chrome 149+' row says the overflow mode 'temporarily switches to clip. The full text is visible during interaction', and the spec permits exactly that ('may treat text-overflow: ellipsis as text-overflow: clip'). No value is returned to script and no new object, event or observable surface is produced; the record is consistent with this being a paint-time switch — its breaking_change field is false and its feature_type is 'Chromium catches up'.

errors.rationale: A rendering-mode switch has no throwing surface and this page documents no failure, fallback or retry path — the #syntax table carries only the before/after rows and the affected-element conditions. FLAGGED GAP, not a clean absolution: the record exposes no error field or failure mode either, so the dimension is inapplicable for want of any error contract rather than because the page documents one; recorded in notes for the implementer.

context.rationale: The at-a-glance table fixes the exposure context: 'Shipped in: Chrome 149 (desktop, Android, WebView, iOS)', 'Status: Platform behaviour change (no new CSS property)', 'Flag: None', and the two source rows (CSS Overflow Level 3 §ellipsis-interaction; ChromeStatus 5146265241387008). The record corroborates the desktop/Android/WebView half exactly (browsers.chrome desktop, android and webview all 149); the iOS entry and the record's status field are two sides carried in notes, not resolved here.

lifecycle.rationale: The page documents a state transition rather than an object lifecycle: at rest the element shows the ellipsis, on interaction the mode 'temporarily switches to clip' with 'The full text is visible during interaction', and the same section states the transition back — 'When focus leaves the element, the ellipsis is restored.' The spec's trigger for that transition is the same one ('When the user is interacting with content (e.g. editing, selecting, scrolling)'). Nothing is constructed, registered or torn down in script.

examples.rationale: The referenced fragment is the page's primary runnable example: a live contenteditable/tabindex box ('clicking into the box below or pressing End will reveal the full text') plus the complete <pre><code> rule it uses — '.label { overflow: hidden; white-space: nowrap; text-overflow: ellipsis; max-width: 260px; }' with the comment that Chrome 149 temporarily switches text-overflow to 'clip'. The section carries a second complete <pre><code> block ('Contenteditable rich text field'), which sits below the next <h3> and therefore outside this fragment. Both examples use the declaration triple MDN requires for text-overflow to have any effect ('To make text overflow its container, you have to set other CSS properties: overflow and white-space').

compatibility.rationale: The browser-support table gives Chrome '149 — all elements (form controls since earlier)', Edge '149 (Chromium)', Firefox 'Partial (form controls only per MDN)' and Safari 'Partial (form controls only)'; the separate 'compatibility notes' table adds the per-browser behaviour detail ('Already behaved this way before Chrome 149. No change.' for form controls, 'Unaffected' for display-only elements, and the Firefox/Safari rows). The Chrome row is corroborated by MDN's text-overflow: ellipsis data ('From version 149, in contenteditable elements, behaves as clip while the element is focused.'); the Firefox cell additionally disagrees with MDN's Firefox note on that same data, and both the Firefox and Safari cells disagree with the record's browser views (ff 'Shipped/Shipping', safari 'Closed Without a Position') — both sides carried in notes, neither adjudicated.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The page documents no security or privacy surface: the interaction reveals text that is already in the DOM and already in the layout, on a direct user gesture, and adds no permission, origin, storage or script-readable surface — #why-it-exists describes only the caret/visibility problem ('could move the caret into invisible content'). FLAGGED GAP, not a clean absolution: the record's security_review_status and privacy_review_status both read 'Pending' (fetched 2026-10-07) and the page carries no security or privacy sentence at all; recorded in notes for the implementer.

CORROBORATED, NOT DIVERGENT: the record's spec_link field is exactly the §ellipsis-interaction URL the page cites; its summary ('When a user interacts (editing or caret navigation) with text which has ‘text-overflow: ellipsis’ set, the text switches temporarily from ellipsis to clip allowing the user to see and interact with the hidden overflow content. This feature applies to all editable and non-editable elements. For form controls (textarea, input), the behavior is already supported.') matches the page's framing and its 'extends this to all elements' claim; and MDN's text-overflow: ellipsis compatibility data records Chrome 'From version 149, in contenteditable elements, behaves as clip while the element is focused.' — the page's 149 milestone and its 'form controls since earlier' phrasing are the same fact. CARRIED DISAGREEMENTS, BOTH SIDES, NEITHER ADJUDICATED (all fetched 2026-10-07; record accurate_as_of 2026-04-27 09:04:47, last updated by shwetabindal@microsoft.com, created 2026-01-20): (1) BROWSER-SUPPORT CELLS — the page's browser-support table reads Firefox 'Partial (form controls only per MDN)' and Safari 'Partial (form controls only)', while the ChromeStatus record the page cites for that table reports browsers.ff.view.text 'Shipped/Shipping' and browsers.safari.view.text 'Closed Without a Position' (its url is https://github.com/WebKit/standards-positions/issues/624, webdev 'No signals'), and MDN's own text-overflow: ellipsis data records Firefox as 'In contenteditable elements, behaves as clip while the element is focused.' — i.e. not form-controls-only, which is the opposite direction from the page's cell while the page attributes that cell to MDN. The page's 'compatibility notes' table hedges the same two rows ('non-form behaviour may vary'; 'Implements this behaviour for form controls.'). (2) SHIP STATUS AND THE iOS CLAIM — #at-a-glance says 'Shipped in: Chrome 149 (desktop, Android, WebView, iOS)' and the lede says 'Chrome 149 temporarily clips the text instead', while the record's browsers.chrome.status.text is 'Proposed' with is_released false; its ship stage (stage_type 260, intent_stage 5) carries desktop_first/android_first/webview_first 149 and ios_first null, and the only iOS milestone anywhere on the record (147) sits on the developer-trial stage (stage_type 230, desktop_first/android_first/ios_first 147). So the iOS half of the page's platform list has no counterpart on the ship stage, and the shipped framing coexists with a 'Proposed' status field. (3) NORMATIVE STRENGTH (the weakest of the three; recorded, not adjudicated — the page's substance is not in dispute) — the page says 'The CSS Overflow spec has always said that text should revert to clipping during user interaction', while §ellipsis-interaction's actual sentence is 'When the user is interacting with content (e.g. editing, selecting, scrolling), the user agent may treat text-overflow: ellipsis as text-overflow: clip' — permissive 'may', not obligative 'should' — and css-overflow-4's ED (https://drafts.csswg.org/css-overflow-4/#ellipsis-interaction, HTTP 200) keeps the same 'may' for 'ellipsis, string values, fade or fade()'.
